decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm's core border and passenger-security capabilities and already shows strong external adoption, so management can learn from clear market feedback and is very unlikely to withdraw it.

Although it builds on the firm's compliance and travel-security knowledge, travel-health requirements appear more temporary by 2024, so management would be relatively likely to redeploy resources if demand has faded.

A cyber security awareness training module fits the firm's training resources and security know-how, giving it enough related knowledge to improve the offer even if early website evidence is still limited.

Behaviour analysis in security is closely related to the firm's specialist detection activities, so despite modest visible traction the firm is likely to retain it and refine it within its established customer base.

Passenger security profiling is highly connected to the firm's aviation and transport-security expertise, but because it may face sensitivity and adoption hurdles management would keep it with more caution than its strongest products.

Document and travel verification are central to integrated security operations, and a dedicated web platform is close enough to the firm's existing capabilities that management would likely continue backing it.
